We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline.

Structure: Two aromatic rings: ring A (para-methyl phenyl) with sulfonamide linking to ring B (phenyl) which has a para-substituted trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph (anilide). Actually the sulfonyl group attaches to ring B at para position? The SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

So ring A: methyl phenyl with sulfonamide N attached to sulfonyl group S(=O)(=O)- attached to ring B (phenyl). Ring B has para substituent: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-N (aniline). So overall three steps: maybe disconnection at amide formation (C=O N), at the double bond formation via Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid), and at sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). So retrosynthesis:

Step1 (forward) amide formation: from carboxylic acid (trans-α,β-unsaturated acid) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). So retro: break amide to give trans-α,β-unsaturated acid (C=O) and aniline.

Step2: Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So retro: break double bond to give aldehyde on ring B and malonic acid.

Step3: Sulfonamide formation: from sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2- attached to ring B) and aniline (ring A). Actually sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to ring A N. So retro: break N-S bond to give sulfonyl chloride attached to ring B and aniline (ring A with NH2). So final precursors: aniline (ring A) with methyl, sulfonyl chloride on ring B, aldehyde on ring B, malonic acid, aniline (ring C). Wait we also need the aniline for amide (c3ccccc3N) which is separate phenyl amine.

Thus final set of starting materials: 1) 4-methyl aniline (para-methyl aniline) (for sulfonamide N). 2) 4-(chlorosulfonyl)phenyl (or 4-chlorosulfonyl phenyl) i.e., 4-chlorosulfonylbenzene (ClSO2-Ph). Actually the sulfonyl chloride attached to ring B (para to the aldehyde). So need 4-chlorosulfonylbenzaldehyde? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to ring B, which also later gets aldehyde and double bond. In retrosynthesis, after step2 we have ring B with sulfonyl chloride and aldehyde? Actually step2 forms the α,β-unsaturated acid on ring B, but the sulfonyl chloride is already attached to ring B before step2? The order of steps: The guidance says reactions enumerated in order they must be applied (forward). So step1: amide formation (carboxylic acid to amide). Step2: Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). Step3: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So forward order: first sulfonamide formation, then Doebner, then amide? Wait they said enumerated in order they must be applied. The hints: carboxylic acid to amide, Doebner modification, sulfonamide formation. So forward: start from precursors, first sulfonamide formation (makes sulfonamide), then Doebner (makes double bond), then amide formation (makes amide). That seems plausible: start with aniline (ring A) + sulfonyl chloride (ring B) -> sulfonamide intermediate (ring A attached to sulfonyl group attached to ring B). Then Doebner: aldehyde on ring B + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid attached to ring B (still sulfonamide present). Then amide coupling with aniline (ring C) to give final product.

Thus retrosynthetic steps (reverse): 1) break amide -> give α,β-unsaturated acid (with sulfonamide) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). 2) break double bond -> give aldehyde (on ring B) + malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). 3) break sulfonamide -> give sulfonyl chloride (on ring B) + aniline (ring A with methyl). So final precursors: 4-methyl aniline, 4-chlorosulfonylbenzaldehyde? Wait sulfonyl chloride attached to ring B which also has aldehyde at para position. The sulfonyl chloride is attached to the same ring as aldehyde? In target, sulfonyl group is attached at para to methyl phenyl? Actually ring B has sulfonyl attached to N (coming from ring A). The sulfonyl group is attached to ring B at position where N attaches (i.e., sulfonyl attached to ring B carbon). The aldehyde is at para to that sulfonyl? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2 attached to S(=O)(=O) from N. The S attached to c2 (the phenyl). The aldehyde is not present; after Doebner, the aldehyde becomes the α,β-unsaturated acid. So before Doebner, the ring B has an aldehyde at that position (para to sulfonyl). So sulfonyl chloride precursor would be 4-chlorosulfonylbenzaldehyde? Actually sulfonyl chloride attached to ring B at the position where N attaches (i.e., para to methyl phenyl? Not needed). The sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring (ring B) at the position where the N attaches. So the precursor is 4-chlorosulfonylbenzaldehyde (ClSO2-Ph-CHO) where the sulfonyl chloride is para to aldehyde? In SMILES, c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2: the sulfonyl attaches at the carbon where N attaches, which is at position 1 of ring B. The aldehyde is at position 4 (para). So yes, we need 4-chlorosulfonylbenzaldehyde (or 4-formylchlorosulfonylbenzene). That is a known compound.

Thus final precursors list: 1) 4-methylaniline (p-toluidine) SMILES: Cc1ccc(N)cc1. 2) 4-chlorosulfonylbenzaldehyde SMILES: O=CC1=CC=C(S(=O)(=O)Cl)C=C1? Actually need correct SMILES: O=CC1=CC=C(S(=O)(=O)Cl)C=C1. That's O=CC1=CC=C(S(=O)(=O)Cl)C=C1. 3) malonic acid SMILES: C(C(=O)O)C(=O)O. 4) aniline (c3ccccc3N) SMILES: c1ccccc1N.

Now we need to construct JSON route with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We haven't retrieved them. Could use generic placeholder? Must be valid IDs from catalog. We can search for templates matching functional groups.

Step3 (sulfonamide formation): search for sulfonamide formation: functional_groups_formed: sulfonamides, functional_groups_broken: primary amines? Actually sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide. So broken: primary amines, acyl chloride? Actually sulfonyl chloride is not acyl chloride but sulfonyl chloride functional group maybe "acyl chloride"? Not in list. But we can search with functional_groups_formed: sulfonamides. Let's try.
